description: Raw WebGPU rendering starter — no three.js, no abstraction. Drives navigator.gpu directly: adapter → device → canvas context → render pipeline → bind groups → render pass. WGSL vertex + fragment shaders draw a colored triangle at 60fps. Foundation for low-level graphics, custom renderers, and engine work.

buildHints.whenToUse: Any product that needs the raw WebGPU API — custom renderers, engine internals, novel rendering techniques (deferred, cluster-forward, raymarching), or shader-driven art where three.js's abstractions get in the way. Pick threejs-game instead if you want a batteries-included 3D scene graph.
firstSteps: Install: `pnpm install` then `pnpm dev` — Vite serves on 5173. Open Chrome 113+, Edge 113+, or Safari 18+; a gradient triangle fills the canvas.
The rendering pipeline is in `src/main.ts` — adapter → device → canvas context config → render pipeline with vertex + fragment WGSL → render pass targeting the swap chain texture.

The shader is a single file at `src/shaders/main.wgsl` containing both the `@vertex` and `@fragment` entry points. Extend by adding vertex buffers (for real meshes) or uniform buffers (for camera/time).
To add a textured quad next: create a GPUTexture, upload an ImageBitmap via `queue.copyExternalImageToTexture`, bind a GPUSampler + texture in a new bind group, sample it in the fragment shader.
Build: `pnpm build` emits static assets to `dist/` — deploy to any static host. WebGPU requires HTTPS in production (localhost is exempt).
gotchas: WebGPU is Chrome/Edge 113+ and Safari 18+ stable. Firefox ships it behind `dom.webgpu.enabled` — always feature-detect `navigator.gpu` and show a fallback UI.

The canvas format from `getPreferredCanvasFormat()` differs between platforms (bgra8unorm on macOS, rgba8unorm elsewhere). Store it once and use it both in `context.configure({ format })` AND the pipeline's `fragment.targets[0].format` — mismatch throws at pipeline creation.
Each frame must call `context.getCurrentTexture().createView()` — the texture is recycled by the swap chain and stale views throw on the next submit.
Canvas resize: set `canvas.width` and `canvas.height` to `window.innerWidth * devicePixelRatio` (cap DPR at 2) and re-call `context.configure()` — ignoring this gives blurry output or wrong viewport.
Always cancel `requestAnimationFrame` on teardown (HMR, route change). WebGPU does not garbage-collect GPU resources; dangling frames leak and eventually crash the tab.
Shader compilation errors are async — call `module.getCompilationInfo()` during development; a broken WGSL module otherwise produces a silent black canvas.
architectureNotes: Create the GPUDevice once per page and reuse it for every pipeline and buffer — `requestDevice()` is expensive.
Pre-create pipelines, bind group layouts, and buffers outside the render loop; only command-buffer construction belongs inside `requestAnimationFrame`.
For multiple passes (shadow + main + post), batch into a single GPUCommandEncoder and submit once per frame — each `queue.submit` has a non-trivial CPU/GPU sync cost.

placeholders.description: WebGPU render bootstrap — device, canvas context, pipeline, bind groups, render loop, resize handling. Extend by adding vertex buffers for real geometry, uniform buffers for camera/time, and textures via `queue.copyExternalImageToTexture`.

Vertex + fragment WGSL. The vertex stage emits a fullscreen-ish triangle from @builtin(vertex_index); the fragment stage outputs a smooth gradient. Replace the positions with a vertex buffer binding for real meshes.
